title: F7a deps+qr module: RSA/OAEP/QR
description:
IMPLEMENT F7 auth module + deps.
DEPS (workspace Cargo.toml): rsa = "0.9", qrcode = "0.14" (md-5 already added by F6).
NEW crates/discord-auth/src/qr.rs:
pub async fn qr_login(save: bool) -> Result<String>
Flow (discordo login/qr/msg.go:32-307; mrarfarf cmd/qr_login.go):
1. Dial wss://remote-auth-gateway.discord.gg/?v=2 (tokio-tungstenite — in crate tree) with browser UA.
2. Gen RSA-2048; send {"op":"init","encoded_public_key":<b64 PKIX SPKI DER>}.
3. nonce_proof -> OAEP-SHA256 decrypt (rand.Reader) -> {"op":"nonce_proof","nonce":<b64 RawURL>}.
4. pending_remote_init -> print ASCII QR of https://discord.com/ra/{fingerprint} to stderr (qrcode crate); keep fingerprint.
5. pending_ticket -> decrypt user_payload -> parse 'discriminator:username' (4 ':' parts -> [1],[3]) -> print 'Waiting for <username>...'.
6. pending_login -> POST https://discord.com/api/v9/users/@me/remote-auth/login body {"ticket":...} headers X-Fingerprint + Referer https://discord.com/login (discordo) -> decrypt encrypted_token -> token.
7. cancel -> error exit. Heartbeat per hello interval.
Save via existing auth save path if save=true.
TEST: unit — RSA-OAEP roundtrip, base64 variants, user_payload parse.
acceptance_criteria: 1. rsa+qrcode deps added. 2. qr_login full op sequence. 3. RSA-OAEP roundtrip unit test. 4. ASCII QR printed. 5. ticket exchange with X-Fingerprint header.

title: db.rs — SQLite schema (guilds/channels/messages/FTS5/sync_state) + WAL
description:
## Background
Offline archive of messages for search/analysis. Schema from langkurt (MIT, verbatim-portable) + jackwener (Apache). Plan §6 has exact CREATE statements.

## Technical Approach
- rusqlite bundled, one connection, WAL + foreign_keys.
- Tables: guilds(id PK,name,icon), channels(id PK,guild_id,name,type,topic,parent_id), messages(id PK,channel_id,guild_id,author_id,author_name,content,timestamp,edited,reaction_count), sync_state(channel_id PK,last_message_id,oldest_message_id,synced_at).
- FTS5 external-content messages_fts(content,author_name) + triggers ai/ad/au.
- Optional attachments(id,message_id,url,filename,content_type,size,local_path) + links.
- Indexes: idx_messages_channel/timestamp/author/reactions.
- Upsert: guild/channel/message = INSERT OR REPLACE; attachment = INSERT OR IGNORE; sync_state ON CONFLICT with CASE max/min (langkurt).
- db.rs module; migrate = ordered statement list, skip duplicate column errors.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Schema creates clean; upserts idempotent; FTS5 triggers sync.

## Test Plan
- Unit: schema migration; upsert dedup (insert same id twice → 1 row); FTS5 trigger inserts.
- Integration: temp-db round-trip.

## Considerations
- Snowflake compare as STRING (safe). guild_id NULL for DM → COALESCE 'DM'.

title: dc sync + dc sync-all — two-phase incremental sync
description:
## Background
Bootstrap + incrementally sync channels to SQLite. Two-phase from langkurt (plan §12, §11). This powers offline search and 'summarize channel' at scale.

## Technical Approach
- dc sync <CHANNEL> [-n 5000]: Phase A forward (after=last_message_id) if state exists; Phase B backward (before=oldest_message_id) resume; persist max/min cursors.
- dc sync-all [-n 200] [--since 30d]: discover all guilds+text channels, sync each bounded (200 default).
- FetchMessages: 400ms base + 0-300ms jitter + 429 backoff 2s→10s cap; page 100; string snowflake cursors; stop_before cutoff for --since.
- ParseSince: date or Nd/d/w/y relative (Escape-Tech regex + langkurt timeutil).
- commands/dc_sync.rs, commands/dc_sync_all.rs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- sync resumes correctly; sync-all bounded; --since filters; rate-limit sleeps visible.

## Test Plan
- Unit: cursor walk (trait fake asserting cursor sequence); ParseSince.
- E2E real token: sync one small channel, sync-all bounded.

## Considerations
- Forum/media channels are containers → sync threads first. Never mass-crawl.
close_reason: M4.2 done: dc sync + dc sync-all two-phase

title: auth auto-detect — Windows DPAPI + LevelDB token extraction

## Background
Auto-discover the user token from local Discord/browser session — no manual paste. From jackwener auth.py + discord-cli-rs auth/windows.rs (MIT, portable).

## Technical Approach
- auth --save: scan %APPDATA%\discord\{discord,ptb,canary}\Local Storage\leveldb + Chrome/Brave/Edge Local Storage.
- Token regexes: [\w-]{24,}\.[\w-]{6}\.[\w-]{27,} and mfa\.[\w-]{84}.
- Windows: Discord desktop tokens DPAPI-encrypted in LevelDB; Chrome/Edge AES-GCM with DPAPI-wrapped key in Local State. Decrypt via CryptUnprotectData (windows crate Win32_Security_Cryptography).
- Validate against GET /users/@me; write/upsert DISCORD_TOKEN into ./.env (jackwener save_token_to_env).
- auth/mod.rs, auth/detect.rs, auth/windows.rs (+ linux.rs, macos.rs stubs/best-effort).

## Acceptance Criteria
- auth --save finds + validates token; writes .env; no token → clear error.

## Test Plan
- Unit: regex matching; .env write/upsert; DPAPI decrypt (mock).
- Manual: run on machine with Discord logged in.

## Considerations
- This is the 'AI uses it for me' convenience — but warn about ToS risk. Never print raw token.

1. fn classify(e: &anyhow::Error) -> u8 (dc.rs):
   Walk e.chain() for crate DiscordError variants -> exit code:
   - DiscordError::PermissionDenied -> exit::FORBIDDEN (4)  [403]
   - DiscordError::NotFound -> exit::NOT_FOUND (3)  [404]
   - DiscordError::RateLimited -> exit::ERROR (1) with 'retry after Ns' message
   - else -> exit::ERROR (1)
   Handlers become ExitCode::from(classify(&e)) + emit_error(code, msg, classify(&e)).
   This makes FORBIDDEN=4 LIVE for the first time (admin ops routinely 403).

2. fn check_confirm(target_desc: &str, action: &str, id: &str, confirm: bool) -> Option<ExitCode> (dc.rs):
   Emits eprintln 'This will {action} {target_desc} ({id}). Add --confirm to proceed.'
   Returns Some(USAGE) when !confirm, else None.
   Single code path for the destructive gate — used by channel/role/emoji/invite delete, kick/ban/unban, perm lock/unlock.
